display_name: Vasse Felix Filius Cabernet Sauvignon, Margaret River
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Vasse Felix's Filius Cabernet Sauvignon sources from 50-year-old estate vines rooted in Margaret River's red gravelly loams, yielding cassis and blackberry concentration at $26. Maritime breezes temper the tannins for immediate appeal, as Halliday's 92 points note the dark fruits and nori savoriness.",
  "wine_summary": "Vasse Felix established Margaret River's first vineyard in 1967, pioneering Cabernet Sauvignon plantings that define the region's Bordeaux-style reds. Filius serves as their value-driven second label, drawing from the same Wilyabrup sites to deliver dense fruit without flagship prices. These wines stand out for balancing power with restraint, thanks to the GI's ironstone and gravel soils fostering deep root systems and flavor intensity.",
  "terroir_expression": "Red gravelly loam and Forest Grove ironstone in Margaret River force vines to root deeply, concentrating cassis, kirsch, and blackberry flavors while imparting a mineral tobacco edge. Loamy gravel over clay retains just enough moisture in the maritime climate—wet winters and Indian Ocean-cooled summers—for even ripening, resulting in supple mid-palate texture and spice notes like cardamom and palo santo. Deep infertile sands add the mint lift Halliday detects, linking geology directly to the wine's savory persistence.",
  "vinification_summary": "Vasse Felix hand-harvests Filius for cool fermentation in stainless steel, followed by malolactic fermentation (which softens acidity into creaminess) and 10-12 months in older French oak to preserve fruit without over-extraction. This approach extracts dense tannins noted in the 91-point 2023 review while keeping the wine approachable young, prioritizing site expression over heavy wood influence.",
  "food_pairing": "Grilled ribeye steak with garlic butter: dense tannins slice through fat, cassis echoes beef juices. Nashville hot chicken sandwich: spice amplifies cardamom and tobacco, supple structure handles heat without clashing. Seared duck breast with cherry reduction: dark fruits mirror the sauce, ironstone minerality cuts richness. Rack of lamb persillade at fine dining: rosemary lifts mint notes, gravel-driven structure matches protein. Cheeseburger with aged cheddar: blackberry depth complements melt, nori savoriness nods to umami.",
  "comparable_wines": "Leeuwin Estate Art Series Cabernet Sauvignon — shares Margaret River gravel for cassis focus and ocean-fresh tannins. Cape Mentelle Cabernet Merlot — similar maritime density with black fruits and spice at comparable pricing. Voyager Estate Cabernet Sauvignon — Wilyabrup ironstone minerality yields parallel tobacco layers.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied Cabernet Sauvignon with dense tannins and savory dark fruit core",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink from release through 2030 for peak fruit integration. Store at 55°F in darkness to preserve color and evolve spice complexity.",
  "value_assessment": "$26 at Spec's positions Filius against Pepper Tree Cabernet ($25) and d'Arenberg The Stump Jump GSM ($24). It outperforms on density and scores, making it a clear buy for structured Aussie red fans. NV consistency seals the deal over vintage variables.",
  "market_position": "Retail shelves at Spec's target casual Cabernet drinkers upgrading from $20 bottles. Steakhouse lists feature it for by-the-glass value in Australia-heavy programs. Margaret River collectors use Filius as an everyday entry before flagship hunts.",
  "insider_take": "Margaret River Cabernet beats Coonawarra for coastal freshness—Filius proves it without excess power. Skip if eucalyptus mint repels you; otherwise, stock up before prices climb. The real edge lies in 2023's palo santo nuance over NV reliability.",
  "aging_potential_years": 10,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 0,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 10,
  "sensory": {

Deep infertile sands add the mint lift Halliday detects, linking geology directly to the wine's savory persistence.

This approach extracts dense tannins noted in the 91-point 2023 review while keeping the wine approachable young, prioritizing site expression over heavy wood influence.
